A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JUICE/RDBLearn research work. Their main text, equations, figures, results, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original RDBLearn benchmark evaluations in Section 6 and an original synthetic feature-mixing experiment averaged over 100 trials in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds author-executed RandGNN comparisons and evaluations on RelBench-v2.

M1.justification: The column-preserving JUICE encoder, parameter-free aggregation procedure, temporal features, and single-table ICL prediction pipeline are unchanged. RandGNN is a comparator; the new usage documentation and prospective agent integrations do not establish changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds five RelBench-v2 tasks: three binary classification tasks and two regression tasks, including beer-churn, brewer-dormant, and beer-ratings-total. This substantially extends the evaluated data coverage beyond the retained RelBench-v1 and 4DBInfer tasks. Rel-arxiv and rel-mimic are explicitly excluded.

E2.justification: RandGNN joins the existing RelBench-v1 classification and regression comparisons. Both RandGNN and Griffin are added to 4DBInfer, where Griffin was previously absent. The new RelBench-v2 comparison includes Griffin, RandGNN, and a supervised GNN; existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces an evaluation control coupling randomly initialized, untrained GNN encodings with the tabular ICL models used by RDBLearn. It also specifies evaluation of Griffin and RandGNN without additional training on RelBench-v2. Existing 10k context sampling, hop choices, development-set model selection, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new RandGNN comparison tests whether performance depends on JUICE featurization rather than merely a strong tabular decoder. Existing hop/backend ablations, synthetic feature-mixing tests, and supervised-versus-ICL analyses are retained. Appendix F.1 additionally mentions favorable preliminary tests with more aggregators, but supplies no supporting results.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the same 100-trial averaging and identical error-bar plots. V2 introduces no additional seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures for the benchmark comparisons.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for RandGNN, Griffin on 4DBInfer, and five RelBench-v2 tasks. For example, new Figure 4 reports user-churn AUCs of 97.81 for RDBLearn and 94.27 for the supervised GNN. Existing RDBLearn scores remain unchanged, including 74.81 mean RelBench-v1 classification AUC; the added RandGNN mean is 70.02. The leakage discussion also corrects 99.61 to 99.62 AUC.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, propositions, equations, and derivations are unchanged. V1 Appendix F matches v2 Appendix G after renumbering. The new contextual caveats do not revise the formal assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions—column-preserving encoding, theoretical support, and RDB prediction without additional training—remain intact. V2 qualifies the label-information wording in the abstract and introduction, and adds a concluding claim about possible advantages of transparent SQL-based features for agentic reasoning.

C2.justification: New Section 3.1 caveats acknowledge historical labels within encoder inputs and external metadata that could justify cross-column feature engineering. V2 also discusses leakage risks from LLM-assisted aggregation, interprets RandGNN findings, and extends the retained ablation's interpretation to competitive performance without validation-based selection.

D1.justification: New Appendix E documents DuckDB/FeatureTools implementation, API arguments, key mappings, cutoff-time semantics, a minimal usage example, and an affiliated skill installation link. These are additional disclosures rather than demonstrated implementation changes. The original repository link is relocated, while checkpoints, hardware, and context limits are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused references and positioning concerning random-weight GNNs, LLM feature engineering and ReFuGe, RelBench-v2, DuckDB, and agentic database reasoning. The established positioning against supervised relational learning and existing RDB foundation models remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds localized caveat and usage explanations, moves the existing stability discussion, renames Conclusions to Discussion, and distinguishes RelBench-v1 from RelBench-v2. Most existing prose and the overall argument structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the RelBench-v2 results display and usage-code figure, expands comparison displays with additional model columns, and redraws the 4DBInfer ranking chart. V1 Figure 10 becomes a reformatted Table 1 with added comparators; existing ablation and appendix plots are retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: RandGNN strengthens empirical assessment of the encoder rationale, and RelBench-v2 broadens validation. The new caveats improve qualification of the argument, while Appendix E makes usage clearer. These provide an incremental overall gain: the added benchmark results remain preliminary and lack run-level uncertainty, and the new agentic and future-performance assertions are not experimentally established.
